evals.name: orphan-enrollment-and-referential-integrity
evals.prompt: We exported our school SIS to OneRoster CSV format. Clever failed our import with 'Foreign key error in enrollments.csv'. Here is a sample: enr_101,cls_chem,usr_4402,student. How do we audit our entire roster for this?
evals.expected_output: The agent specifies loading all primary keys (sourcedId) from users.csv and classes.csv into memory sets, and iterating through enrollments.csv to ensure every userSourcedId and classSourcedId resolves to an existing entity. It flags orphan references explicitly and provides a Python validation script.

evals.name: utf8-bom-and-excel-export-sanitization
evals.prompt: After our admin edited users.csv in Microsoft Excel, our automated sync started failing claiming 'Column sourcedId missing'. The file clearly starts with sourcedId on the first line.
evals.expected_output: The agent diagnoses the classic Excel UTF-8 Byte Order Mark (BOM) trap: Excel prepends \xEF\xBB\xBF to the file, causing parsers to read '\ufeffsourcedId' instead of 'sourcedId'. It provides a one-line Python/bash sanitizer to strip the BOM and re-encode to clean UTF-8.

evals.name: bulk-vs-delta-mode-strictness
evals.prompt: Our manifest.csv declares propertyName 'oneroster.version,1.1' and 'file.users,bulk'. However, our SIS export script includes a dateLastModified column with ISO timestamps and a status column with 'tobedeleted' on users.csv. Is this compliant?
evals.expected_output: The agent strictly states this is non-compliant with OneRoster v1.1. In bulk exchange mode, files represent a full snapshot and must NOT contain dateLastModified or delta status markers. It explains that mixing bulk and delta headers causes ingestion parsers to either drop records or crash, and instructs the user to either remove the delta columns or switch the manifest declaration to delta mode.
